rows.m: Availability of metropolitan-area GDP for LA-Long Beach-Anaheim MSA
rows.n: IRREGULARITY IR-01: BEA has discontinued GDP and personal income statistics for MSAs, micropolitan areas, metropolitan divisions and CSAs. Any projection that relied on MSA-level GDP must now be rebuilt on COUNTY-level GDP. Published here as a documented change of official methodology, not an inference.

rows.m: LA County — occupations with fastest projected job growth
rows.v: Nurse Practitioners 5,890 -> 9,170 (+35.8%); Nurse Anesthetists 540 -> 770 (+29.9%); Travel Agents 2,150 -> 3,060 (+29.7%); Physician Assistants 2,710 -> 3,810 (+28.9%); Physical Therapist Assistants 2,260 -> 3,180 (+28.9%)
rows.s: California EDD, Labor Market Information Division — Los Angeles County Profile
rows.n: The official state 10-year occupational projection window (2022-2032) ENDS BEFORE the 2030-2035 lease expiry. Growth is concentrated in health care, not in the sectors that generate central-LA daytime office traffic. IRREGULARITY IR-04: no official projection series extends through 2035.

rows.m: LA County — commuting flows (place of residence to place of work)
rows.v: 4,429,523 residents working inside LA County; 196,169 LA County residents working in Orange County; 180,250 Orange County residents working in LA County
rows.s: California EDD, Labor Market Information Division — Los Angeles County Profile
rows.n: Intra-county commuting dominates. A central-LA site serves residents and in-county commuters, not cross-county flows.
